ai.title: Add eval planner latency tracking
ai.summary: Eval planner now tracks and reports latency metrics. Implementation wraps `withTestRepo` calls in `evals/subagents/eval-planner.ts` with `Date.now()` timestamps, propagating `plannerLatencyMs` through agent output, JSON results, and console stats (avg/min/max/median). SDK `handleToolCall` error path in `sdk/src/run.ts` fixed to mutate `result` variable instead of returning early, ensuring consistent output structure.

eli5.text: The system now records how long each AI analysis task takes to complete and includes that timing information in its reports. If you work with these analysis tasks, you will notice timing statistics like average and maximum durations appearing alongside scores and feedback in the results. A related internal consistency fix means error outputs now follow the same format as successful ones, so automated systems handling these tasks receive uniformly shaped responses regardless of outcome.

ai.title: Remove ASYNCAGENTSENABLED
ai.summary: Removed `ASYNC_AGENTS_ENABLED` flag and `endUserInput` function from `backend/src/live-user-inputs.ts`, `backend/src/run-agent-step.ts`, `backend/src/websockets/server.ts`, `backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts`, `common/src/old-constants.ts`, `npm-app/src/cli.ts`, and `npm-app/src/client.ts`. Code now unconditionally calls `cancelUserInput` and uses single `userInputId` for validation, dropping `nonCancelledUserInputIds` array logic in `npm-app/src/client.ts`. This cleanup removes dead code for async agent handling that was permanently enabled.

eli5.text: The app used to ask a hidden yes/no question, "are async agents enabled?", to decide whether to fully stop listening for your typing when you hit the cancel button or moved on. That question only ever had one answer (yes), so the app now always fully stops listening to your previous typing in a single, simpler step, instead of keeping a running list of inputs and sometimes leaving old ones half-alive. If you were watching closely, you'd notice the cancel button now behaves like a clean reset with no leftover background chatter.

ai.title: Terminal command check requires tool access
ai.summary: Moved terminal command detection in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` to occur after agent template resolution. Logic now guards execution with `mainAgentTemplate.toolNames.includes('run_terminal_command')`. Prevents `checkTerminalCommand` invocation for agents lacking terminal tool access.

eli5.text: When the assistant receives a message that looks like a direct terminal command (like 'ls /tmp'), it now only tries to run it directly if the specific assistant configuration actually has the terminal tool available. Previously the assistant would attempt the shortcut check for every configuration, which could cause errors for assistants that don't have terminal access. If you're using an assistant that doesn't include the terminal tool, that command path will now correctly skip the shortcut and proceed normally; if your assistant does include it, behavior is unchanged. Effective today.

ai.title: Reorganize thinker agents into thinker directory
ai.summary: Moved thinker agent definitions from .agents/deep-thinking and .agents/factory into .agents/thinker. Deleted gemini-thinker-high.ts and standalone thinker.ts, replacing factory-based instantiation with direct exports. Updated deep-thinker.ts, deepest-thinker.ts, gemini-thinker.ts, gpt5-thinker.ts, and sonnet-thinker.ts paths. Refactored thinker.ts to remove AGENT_PERSONAS dependency, hardcode model to openai/gpt-5, add inheritParentSystemPrompt, remove toolNames, and update instructions.

eli5.text: The internal team moved all the deep-thinking helper definitions into a single dedicated folder, so anything that looks for those helpers now uses the new path. Two old helper files were removed, and the remaining ones had their instructions cleaned up to no longer depend on shared persona settings. If you looked at this change today, you’d see one folder of related helpers instead of scattered ones, but the actual thinking behavior you rely on stays the same.

ai.title: Add decomposing thinker agent to base2 workflow
ai.summary: Introduced `decomposing-thinker` and `thinker-sonnet` agents to the base2 coding workflow. `base2.ts` now spawns a thinker for insights before the planner, expanding the toolset with `code_search`. The `read-only-commander` was restricted from spawning agents to enforce stricter read-only boundaries.

eli5.text: When you ask the coding assistant to tackle a tricky problem, it now pauses to think through several different angles of the problem before it starts planning, like having a careful brainstorming step before making a to-do list. This slower upfront thinking is available right now when the assistant runs its standard multi-step coding workflow. The assistant can also search through code examples more thoroughly during its research phase, and the read-only helper that explores your files can no longer launch other assistants, keeping it strictly in observation mode.

ai.title: Remove async agent manager mocks from loop-agent-steps tests
ai.summary: Deleted asyncAgentManager mocks and related test cases in `backend/src/__tests__/loop-agent-steps.test.ts`. Removed specific test for async agent message handling during `runLoopAgentSteps`. Adjusted formatting for remaining test calls.

eli5.text: The team cleaned up the testing setup for the assistant's step-by-step workflow, removing old fake placeholder code that simulated background helpers, along with a test case that checked how those helpers behaved during a run. This is purely behind-the-scenes work to keep tests accurate and maintainable, so you wouldn't notice any difference in how the software works today.

ai.title: Remove unused liveUserInputs.endUserInput spy
ai.summary: Removes `liveUserInputs.endUserInput` spy mocks from `read-docs-tool.test.ts` and `run-agent-step-tools.test.ts`. The `endUserInput` method is no longer invoked in these test scenarios. Scope limited to backend test files.

eli5.text: The backend test suite no longer pretends that the assistant ends a user interaction in two specific test files. If you looked at those tests, you'd see the fake code that acted out ending a user turn has been taken out, leaving the other mock behaviors in place. This is internal housekeeping with no effect on what you experience.

ai.title: Fix memory leaks in XML conversion
ai.summary: XML conversion now calls `xmlStreamParser.destroy()` during teardown. `addListener` replaced by `on` for conversion events to prevent listener accumulation. Affects `npm-app/src/client.ts` and `npm-app/src/display/markdown-renderer.ts`.

eli5.text: When you stop a long-running operation, the program now properly shuts down the background process that was converting XML data, instead of leaving it running and slowly consuming memory. The program also switched to a slightly different method for tracking window resize events, which prevents duplicate entries from piling up over time. You wouldn't notice these changes directly while using the app, but they keep memory usage from growing unnecessarily during extended sessions.

ai.title: Add stepPrompt to base2 agent config
ai.summary: Added stepPrompt to .agents/base2/base2.ts with reminder to spawn researcher-file-explorer, decomposing-planner, and reviewer-max agents. Removed decomposing-thinker step from workflow, reducing sequential steps from 8 to 7. Scope limited to base2 agent configuration file.

eli5.text: The assistant now gets a short reminder baked into its setup telling it to automatically bring in three helper agents: one to explore your codebase, one to plan the work, and one to review the final result. This drops one middle step from the assistant's normal eight-step workflow, so it takes one fewer turn to get from start to finished review. If you're running this version, the reminder will show up in any task that uses the base2 configuration; if you're on an older snapshot, you won't see it.

ai.title: Wrap stepPrompt in system-reminder tags
ai.summary: stepPrompt values wrapped in `<system-reminder>` tags during prompt generation. Prevents agent misinterpreting step prompts as user input. Internal change in `backend/src/templates/strings.ts`. Conditional wrapping applies only when `promptType.type === 'stepPrompt'` and `agentState.agentType` is present.

eli5.text: When the assistant receives a step-by-step instruction during a task, that instruction is now wrapped in special tags so the assistant recognizes it as guidance rather than a new message from you. Previously, the assistant might have mistaken these internal instructions for your input, causing confusion about whether you had spoken again. You would not notice this directly, but it helps prevent the assistant from misinterpreting its own workflow as your requests.

ai.title: Add empty agent-runtime package scaffold
ai.summary: Created new `@codebuff/agent-runtime` workspace package with `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, and empty `src/index.ts`. Backend now depends on `@codebuff/agent-runtime` via `workspace:*`. Root `tsconfig.json` maps `@codebuff/agent-runtime/*` to `./packages/agent-runtime/src/*`. Package exports use Bun-compatible module resolution with `type: module` and `sideEffects: false`.

eli5.text: A new, still-empty building block called the agent-runtime was added to the project's shared toolkit, and the main backend now lists it as a dependency it expects to use. If you looked at the project's configuration files today, you'd see references to this new package, but because its source code is empty, it doesn't actually do anything yet, it's just scaffolding waiting to be filled in.

ai.title: agent-runtime types, logger param
ai.summary: Agent Runtime now requires a `logger` parameter in `startAgentRun`, `finishAgentRun`, and `addAgentStep`. New `Logger` and function types (`StartAgentRunFn`, etc.) are exported from `packages/agent-runtime/src/types`. Backend functions satisfy these types via `satisfies` keyword. Callers in `run-agent-step.ts` and `run-programmatic-step.ts` updated to pass the logger.

eli5.text: When the assistant starts, finishes, or records a step in an agent run, it now always receives a logger so it can write debug, info, warning, and error messages through that single consistent object instead of a hard-coded one. This lets callers such as the step loop and programmatic step runner pass in their own logger, so log messages stay tied to the right run and the code can be tested with controlled output.

ai.title: Extract shared types into @codebuff/types package
ai.summary: Created @codebuff/types package to centralize Logger and database types, moving them from @codebuff/agent-runtime. Updated backend/src/agent-run.ts to import types from @codebuff/types/database and refactored function signatures to use Parameters/ReturnType helpers. Added @codebuff/types as a dependency to common/package.json. Renamed LoggerFunction to LoggerFn in packages/types/src/logger.ts.

eli5.text: You might notice that logging messages and database-related definitions now live in one shared location instead of being tied specifically to the agent runtime component. The agent run startup and completion functions have been simplified to reference these central types directly rather than defining their own. Nothing about how agents actually run has changed, it's just cleaner organization behind the scenes.

ai.title: initAnalytics accepts injected logger
ai.summary: initAnalytics signature updated to accept { logger: Logger } instead of importing global logger. Backend entrypoint passes explicit logger instance during initialization. Changes span common/src/analytics.ts and backend/src/index.ts. Decouples analytics from static module state for cleaner dependency injection.

eli5.text: When you start up the assistant, it now uses a logging tool that is passed in from the outside instead of reaching into a shared toolbox. This is purely behind-the-scenes housekeeping to keep the parts more independent; you won't notice any change in how things work.

ai.title: trackEvent signature refactored to accept logger
ai.summary: Refactored `trackEvent` in `common/src/analytics.ts` to accept a single object argument including a `logger` instance. Updated all call sites in backend (`message-cost-tracker`, `run-agent-step`, `xml-stream-parser`, `websocket-action`) and packages (`billing`) to pass the logger explicitly. `initializeServer` in `web` now requires a logger parameter to propagate this dependency to `initAnalytics`.

eli5.text: When the assistant records an analytics event (like counting tool calls or user input), it now passes along the running log alongside the data instead of relying on the event-recorder to fetch its own log. This means every recorded event is tied to the correct log, so errors and usage stats show up in the right place instead of possibly ending up detached or mislabeled. If you look at the logs, events will still appear, but they now travel as a single bundled package rather than separate pieces handed off one at a time.

ai.title: Remove unused analytics and API key crypto code
ai.summary: Deleted `logError` from `common/src/analytics.ts` and removed `common/src/api-keys/crypto.ts` entirely. Updated `common/knowledge.md` to drop references to the deprecated encryption utilities. This cleanup removes dead code for error logging and API key storage that is no longer used by calling environments.

eli5.text: The app removed two pieces of old, unused code that were quietly failing to do anything: a helper that tried to log errors through an analytics service it could never reach, and a set of utilities meant to encrypt and store API keys that no part of the product was actually calling. If you looked at the settings or logs, you would notice nothing changed because nothing was reading or using that code to begin with. This cleanup only deletes dead code and updates the internal documentation, so it is safe and live today with no effect on how the app behaves.

ai.title: withSerializableTransaction takes logger via options object
ai.summary: common/src/db/transaction.ts: withSerializableTransaction signature changes from positional (callback, context) to single options object { callback, context, logger }. logger injected as parameter, imported from @codebuff/types/logger. packages/billing/src/balance-calculator.ts and org-billing.ts updated to pass logger at call sites. Internal refactor. No user-facing behavior change.

eli5.text: When you buy or use credits, the system writes a safe record of the transaction so money isn't lost or duplicated. That record-writing step now receives its logging details directly as an argument instead of looking them up itself, which is an internal housekeeping change. Nothing about how you buy or spend credits changes; the behind-the-scenes code is just tidier now. This is already live in today's app.

ai.title: Refactor agent validation to accept logger
ai.summary: Agent validation functions (`validateAgents`, `collectAgentIds`, `validateSpawnableAgents`) now require a `logger` instance via a unified params object. This replaces implicit global logger imports, enabling dependency injection and testability. Updates propagate to `backend/src/templates/agent-registry.ts` and web API routes (`publish`, `validate`). New `ParamsOf` utility type added in `packages/types/src/common.ts`.

eli5.text: When you publish or validate an agent (like adding a custom helper to your workspace), the system now needs to be explicitly handed its logging tool instead of grabbing one it keeps around behind the scenes. Think of it like a restaurant kitchen: previously, every station would sneak over to a shared spice rack to log notes whenever it needed; now, the manager must hand each station its own labeled spice kit at the start of the shift. You won't notice this directly, but if you ever look at the validation process logs, things should be slightly cleaner and more predictable, since each step is using its own designated tool rather than reaching into a shared, invisible supply closet.

ai.title: logSyncFailure signature change to object param with logger
ai.summary: Refactored logSyncFailure in common/src/util/sync-failure.ts to accept a single object parameter including a logger instance instead of positional arguments. Callers in backend/src/llm-apis/message-cost-tracker.ts, packages/billing/src/grant-credits.ts, and web/src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/auth-options.ts updated to pass logger. Removes direct logger import from sync-failure module, enforcing dependency injection for logging.

eli5.text: When Stripe, the payment provider, has trouble syncing your usage data, the system now records that failure more consistently. Previously, the way failures were reported was inconsistent across different parts of the app, like when creating a customer or granting credits. The developers cleaned up how these errors are passed along so they all use the same reporting method, making it easier to track and debug payment-related issues. This is a behind-the-scenes improvement to keep the billing system reliable.

ai.title: BigQuery client functions accept explicit logger parameter
ai.summary: setupBigQuery, insertTrace, insertRelabel, and insertMessage now require a logger instance via destructured object arguments instead of importing a global logger. Callers in backend/src, scripts/ft-file-selection, and packages/bigquery/src/client.ts updated to pass the active logger. packages/bigquery/package.json adds @codebuff/types as a dependency for the Logger type.

eli5.text: If you looked at the logs from the assistant's data-storage system, you'd now see cleaner, per-action details instead of a jumbled mix of messages from different parts of the system. The system that saves the assistant's work to a database now requires each tool or process to pass along its own specific logging details (like where it's coming from and what's important to track), rather than all tools sharing one generic, global log. This is a behind-the-scenes change for the engineers maintaining the platform: it makes it easier for them to trace issues and debug problems in the future. You wouldn't see any new features or performance changes, but it improves the reliability of the backend's internal monitoring. It is live today for all internal developers working on the system.
